mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over the next month reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over a 20-day horizon.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during pre-trend periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in consumer demand (GDPC1) create a dual pressure that elevates risk premia and suppresses S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while GDPC1 decreases over the next 3 months
regime_hint: labor market softening with weak demand
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive despite the combined signal (p-value < 0.05 in a two-tailed test).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below the 50th percentile of the past 12 months signals a demand shortfall that accelerates equity discounting, yielding negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p-value > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for three consecutive months reduces expectations of future rate hikes, prolonging a risk-off environment that drags down S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during high-inflation periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 4%, the anticipation of higher borrowing costs elevates the cost of capital for equities, producing a negative 20-day forward return signal.
candidate_trigger: 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 4%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative in the identified window (p-value > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous surge in job openings (not directly observable in the provided catalog but implied by labor dynamics) and a decline in payrolls (PAYEMS) suggests a labor market imbalance that raises equity risk premia, pushing 60-day forward returns to the negative.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain non-negative despite the labor signal (p-value > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive 2-week decline in manufacturing activity (implied by INDPRO) followed by a rebound below trend indicates weakening demand, which amplifies discounting and results in negative 20-day forward S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO drops for 2 weeks then rebounds below 2021 Q1 median
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p-value > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 2%), the lower discount rate applied to future cash flows increases the present value of equities, producing positive 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during tight-money periods (p-value > 0.1).
